steps.tx: Genetic susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis maps predominantly to the **shared epitope**, a conserved amino acid sequence in the third hypervariable region of **HLA-DRB1** alleles including DRB1*0401 and DRB1*0404. Cigarette smoking and mucosal inflammation in genetically susceptible individuals trigger post-translational protein citrullination. This interaction produces high-affinity **anti-citrullinated protein antibodies** or ACPA years before clinical joint inflammation emerges.
steps.say: Rheumatoid arthritis susceptibility maps to the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope. Cigarette smoking in susceptible individuals promotes protein citrullination and triggers high-affinity anti-CCP antibodies.

rows: Precedes arthritis by up to 10 years

steps.tx: Enzymatic conversion of arginine residues to citrulline is mediated by calcium-dependent **peptidylarginine deiminase** enzymes **PAD2** and **PAD4**. Citrullination alters protein electrical charge, allowing neoepitopes to fit into HLA-DRB1 antigen-binding grooves. Porphyromonas gingivalis expresses bacterial **PPAD**, providing a mechanistic link between periodontal disease, neoepitope generation, and systemic autoimmunity.
steps.say: Peptidylarginine deiminase enzymes convert neutral arginine into citrulline residues. Bacterial PPAD from periodontal infection also generates citrullinated neoepitopes.

nodes.label: PAD2, PAD4, or bacterial PPAD activation

steps.tx: The **2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria** classify definite rheumatoid arthritis using a scoring threshold of **6 or more points** out of 10. Criteria assess joint involvement with up to **5 points**, serology including **rheumatoid factor** and ACPA with up to **3 points**, symptom duration of **6 weeks or more** earning **1 point**, and abnormal acute-phase reactants contributing **1 point**.
steps.say: The 2010 ACR and EULAR criteria classify definite rheumatoid arthritis with a score of 6 or more points. Points evaluate joint distribution, serology, symptom duration, and acute phase reactants.

vis.alt: 2010 ACR-EULAR classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis
vis.caption: The 2010 ACR-EULAR criteria classify rheumatoid arthritis using a 10-point scoring algorithm. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The rheumatoid **synovial pannus** is an invasive, hyperplastic fibrovascular tissue that attaches directly to articular cartilage and subchondral bone. Activated **fibroblast-like synoviocytes** exhibit tumor-like autonomous behavior, secreting destructive matrix metalloproteinases **MMP-1**, **MMP-3**, and **MMP-13**, alongside cathepsins that degrade type II collagen and proteoglycan aggrecan matrices.
steps.say: The invasive rheumatoid synovial pannus destroys cartilage and bone. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes secrete matrix metalloproteinases that degrade type II collagen and aggrecan.

vis.alt: Rheumatoid synovial pannus and articular bone destruction
vis.caption: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes and inflammatory pannus drive cartilage and bone erosion. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Marginal bone erosion at the cartilage-pannus junction is driven by **receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand** or **RANKL**. Synovial T cells and activated synoviocytes express high levels of RANKL, binding **RANK** on osteoclast precursors. Macrophage colony-stimulating factor and TNF-alpha synergistically drive osteoclast differentiation, producing irreversible subchondral **bone erosions**.
steps.say: Receptor activator of NF-kappa B ligand stimulates osteoclast differentiation at the cartilage junction. Synovial RANKL binding to RANK produces characteristic marginal bone erosions.

steps.tx: Early rheumatoid arthritis presents with symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis predominantly involving metacarpophalangeal, proximal interphalangeal, and metatarsophalangeal joints. Inflammatory **morning stiffness** persists for **30 to 60 minutes** or longer. A critical clinical hallmark is sparing of the **distal interphalangeal joints** and thoracolumbar spine, distinguishing rheumatoid arthritis from primary nodal osteoarthritis.
steps.say: Early rheumatoid arthritis causes symmetric MCP and PIP swelling with morning stiffness exceeding 30 to 60 minutes. Sparing of the DIP joints differentiates RA from osteoarthritis.

left.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
points: Symmetrical MCP, PIP, and wrist synovitis
Morning stiffness lasting over 30 to 60 minutes
Elevated ESR, CRP, RF, and ACPA

right.title: Osteoarthritis
points: Heberden DIP and Bouchard PIP nodes

steps.tx: Untreated persistent synovitis produces classic deformities. Tendon stretching and volar subluxation cause **ulnar deviation** at metacarpophalangeal joints. PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion creates the **swan-neck deformity**. PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension produces the **boutonniere deformity**. Radial subluxation of the first MCP with hyperextension of the interphalangeal joint forms the **hitchhiker thumb**.
steps.say: Chronic untreated rheumatoid synovitis causes ulnar deviation at the knuckles. Tendon damage produces characteristic swan-neck, boutonniere, and hitchhiker thumb deformities.

rows: Volar plate laxity, lateral band slip
Central slip rupture of extensor tendon

steps.tx: Emerging post-translational autoantibodies provide prognostic refinement. **Anti-carbamylated protein antibodies** or anti-CarP and anti-acetylated protein antibodies identify patients with severe erosive progression. Notably, anti-CarP antibodies occur in **16 percent to 30 percent** of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis patients lacking both rheumatoid factor and ACPA, predicting worse radiographic joint destruction.
steps.say: Anti-carbamylated protein antibodies identify patients with aggressive erosive disease. Anti-CarP antibodies occur in seronegative individuals and predict severe radiographic progression.
